UNCERTAINTIES: NONE IF YOU WOULD LIKE TO SHARE ANY FEEDBACK ABOUT THIS REPORT OR HAVE QUESTIONS, PLEASE CONTACT THE OPERATIONAL ANALYST AT (301) 683-1403 OR SEND TO OCEANMAP@NOAA.GOV. EMAIL ALERTS ARE AVAILABLE ONLY FOR FEDERAL AND STATE GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS INVOLVED IN RESPONSE EFFORTS. REQUESTS TO BE ADDED TO THE EMAIL ALERTS SHOULD ALSO BE SENT TO OCEANMAP@NOAA.GOV. MARINA STAFF MADE THE OBSERVATION FROM PIER A, WHILE THE VESSEL WAS ANCHORED ABOUT 150' AWAY. ANOTHER VESSEL, A U.S. NAVY TUG, SKENANDOA WAS ANCHORED NEARBY. PIER A IS A LARGE 300' LONG ELEVATED COMMERCIAL PIER. MARINA STAFF REPORTED THAT THE SHEEN APPEARED TO BE COMING FROM THE EIGIL B. AND NOT FROM THE SKENANDOA. MARINA STAFF HAD A REASONABLE SUSPICION TO BELIEVE THAT THE EIGIL B. WAS THE SOURCE OF THE SHEEN BUT COULD NOT VERIFY IT. MARINA OFFICE STAFF PHONED THE OWNER/OPERATOR AND INQUIRED ABOUT THE SHEEN. THEY STATED IN SUBSTANCE, ONLY, THAT THERE WAS ANOTHER VESSEL NEARBY. THEY STATED THAT THEY WERE UNDER WAY AND HAD DEPARTED THE MARINA. MARINA STAFF REPORTED THAT WHEN THE EIGIL B. DEPARTED THE MARINA, THE SHEEN WAS DISPERSED BY THE PROPELLER WASH AS THE VESSEL MOVED THROUGH IT. PHOTOS OF THE SHEEN WERE TAKEN BY MARINA STAFF.
